Outbreak narrative (fictional, for demonstration) — Nord-Kivu, Butembo and Katwa health zones

Overview of early seeding in Butembo/health area of Katsya
- SYN001 (musa katembo), male farmer, 42, resident of Mususa in Katsya (Butembo). Illness began 03/03/2026 after a community market exposure; deceased 17/03/2026; confirmed. This patient anchors the first chain in Katsya. He had regular activity at the Katsya market and moved produce between Mususa and neighboring stalls.
- Secondary infections attributed to SYN001:
  - SYN002 (kalenda masika), female market vendor, 36, from Katsya village, onset 08/03/2026, recovered 25/03/2026; confirmed. Most probable source: household contact with SYN001. Contacts listed: SYN001 and SYN005. She later became the likely source of SYN005.
  - SYN003 (patrick kavira), male student, 15, from Bubange, onset 10/03/2026, recovered 26/03/2026; probable. Reported school contact with SYN001; classification reflects some uncertainty.
  - SYN004 (salima mwamba), female pastor, 60, from Misavu, onset 09/03/2026; deceased 22/03/2026; confirmed. She preached after visiting the same market window as SYN001 and is linked to a church cluster.

Investigator note on SYN001 cluster
- The market exposure explaining SYN001 remains plausible and consistent with his movements in Katsya. Infections in a household vendor (SYN002), a student (SYN003), and a pastor (SYN004) show the early geographic and occupational spread within the same health area.

Health area snapshots (brief)
- Katsya (Butembo): SYN001 → SYN002, SYN003, SYN004; onward to SYN006–SYN009.
- Kyangike (Butembo): healthcare and funeral transmission involving SYN008–SYN013.
- Malende/Ngengere (Butembo): SYN014 core with household (SYN015–SYN017), community suspect (SYN018), and nosocomial (SYN019–SYN020, plus SYN061).
- Mama Musayi (Butembo): SYN021 core with family/funeral (SYN022–SYN023), community/occupational cross-overs (SYN024), and HCW household (SYN025–SYN026); later traditional healer seed (SYN080–SYN082).
- Makerere (Katwa): SYN031 core with household/HCW spillovers (SYN032–SYN036, SYN041–SYN045, SYN050–SYN051).
- Masiki (Katwa): church/funeral sequences (SYN037–SYN040, and SYN068–SYN069).
- Vighole (Katwa): market-to-household (SYN047–SYN048).
- Mukuna (Katwa): market-to-funeral (SYN053–SYN054).
- Masuli (Katwa): market/home care (SYN058–SYN060).
- Kivika (Katwa): workplace/home (SYN071–SYN072).
- Wanamahika (Katwa): market/home (SYN074–SYN075) with nearby school/community signals (SYN049, SYN084).
- Vutike/Vuvatsi (Butembo): community/church (SYN062–SYN066).
- Vulindi (Butembo): community-to-HCW-to-household (SYN030 → SYN076 → SYN077).

Selected individual notes
- SYN032 and SYN050 were both confirmed and associated with SYN031; each had a probable pediatric household case (SYN035 and SYN051 respectively).
- SYN027 and SYN037 were pastors (Mondo and Masiki), both confirmed and both deceased (SYN027 on 21/04/2026; SYN037 on 26/04/2026), each seeding small church-based clusters (SYN028 and SYN038–SYN040).
- SYN058 and SYN064, both confirmed and deceased, illustrate late-April to early-May amplification points in Masuli and Vuvatsi respectively, with secondary household and church contacts (SYN059–SYN060, SYN065–SYN066).
- SYN024 and SYN083 remain under treatment at last report, both confirmed or suspected respectively, with community exposure histories referencing earlier nodes (SYN021/SYN014 and SYN027/SYN031). Their outcomes and final link assignments were pending at the time of compilation.

Closing investigator note
- The linelist shows heterogeneous transmission routes—market, church, healthcare, household, workplace, and funeral exposure—across health areas in Butembo and Katwa. While several chains (e.g., from SYN001, SYN014, SYN021, SYN031, SYN037, SYN058, SYN064, SYN074, SYN080) are well supported, a minority remain suspected or probable (e.g., SYN043, SYN046, SYN052, SYN055, SYN070, SYN073, SYN078, SYN079, SYN083, SYN084), reflecting incomplete recall or overlapping exposure windows. All dates, classifications, outcomes, and locations align with the synthetic linelist provided.
